## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to translate security requirements into policy-as-code and integrate it into CI/CD with runtime enforcement.

## Key Concepts
- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Rego policy
- Pod security primitives: hostNetwork, hostPID, privileged, runAsNonRoot
- CI validation: gatekeeper-audit or dashboard checks, and runtime admission

## Code Example
```rego
package gatekeeper.k8spriv
violation[{"msg":"privileged containers not allowed"}] {
  input.review.object.kind == "Pod"
  some i
  container := input.review.object.spec.containers[i]
  container.securityContext.privileged == true
}
violation[{"msg":"disallow hostNetwork"}] {
  input.review.object.kind == "Pod"
  input.review.object.spec.hostNetwork == true
}
violation[{"msg":"disallow hostPID"}] {
  input.review.object.kind == "Pod"
  input.review.object.spec.hostPID == true
}
```

- How would you extend this to cover initContainers?
- How would you test edge cases like multi-container pods with mixed securityContexts?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to model cross-tenant network security and policy-driven enforcement across clouds. It evaluates how candidates express data-plane constraints in policy code and tie them to manifest checks.

- Default-deny egress via NetworkPolicy

```yaml
# Kyverno policy skeleton
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-tenant-egress
spec:
  rules:

    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment"]
    validate:
      message: "Deployment requires a matching TenantNetworkPolicy"
      pattern:
        metadata:
          annotations:
            tenant.k8s.io/tenant: "*"
```

- How would you test this with a failing manifest and a passing manifest?
- How would you handle tenants with overlapping namespaces or exceptions?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests mastery of policy as code, multi-tenant security, and scalable validation in production Kubernetes clusters.

## Key Concepts

- OPA Gatekeeper: ConstraintTemplates and ConstraintDefinitions
- Namespace defaults: ResourceQuota, LimitRange
- Pod security: runAsNonRoot, runAsUser, readOnlyRootFilesystem, capabilities
- Image security: allowlist + cosign signing
- Network isolation: default NetworkPolicy per Namespace
- Validation: Gatekeeper audits and kubectl describe

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (simplified)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8srequirement
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sRequirement
  targets:
  - target: AdmissionReview
    rego: |
      package k8srequirement
      # minimal rule placeholder
```

```yaml
# ConstraintDefinition (simplified)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sRequirement
metadata:
  name: k8srequirement
spec:
  match:
   Kinds:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        kinds: ["Pod"]
```

```yaml
# Compliant Pod manifest (simplified)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: compliant-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: registry.example.com/app:1.0.0
    securityContext:
      runAsNonRoot: true
      runAsUser: 1000
      allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
    volumeMounts: []
  securityContext:
    runAsNonRoot: true
    runAsUser: 1000
```

## Why This Is Asked
Assesses practical CI gating, SBOM generation, and license compliance in a mono-repo.

## Key Concepts
- SBOM generation with Syft
- SPDX license checks and whitelisting
- Per-service CI gates in a mono-repo
- Interpreting SBOM/license failures

## Code Example
```yaml
name: SBOM and License Gate
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build image
        run: |
          echo "build service image"
      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: |
          syft image:myorg/service:sha -o json > sbom.json
      - name: Upload SBOM
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
        with:
          name: sbom.json
          path: sbom.json
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of identity-based runtime access control in Kubernetes, integrating SPIRE, OPA Gatekeeper, and admission/mutating webhooks for auditing. It also evaluates plan for cross-cloud (Snowflake/IBM) data workloads and secure Spark job execution.

## Key Concepts
- SPIRE workload identity and attestation
- OPA Gatekeeper constraint templates and validation hooks
- Kubernetes RBAC and API access control
- Mutating webhook for audit sidecars
- Validation strategy with compliant vs noncompliant pods

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (example): OPA-based API access gate
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sapiaiaccess
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sAPIAccess
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |-
      package k8sapiaiaccess
      violate["API access denied: identity not whitelisted"] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        identity := input.review.object.metadata.annotations["spire.identity"]
        not identity_in_allowlist(identity)
      }
      
      # allowlisted identities (simplified)
      identity_in_allowlist(id) {
        id == "spiffe://cluster.local/ns/default/sa/spark-sa"
      }
```

```yaml
# Compliant Pod (SPIRE-identity annotated)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: compliant-spark
  annotations:
    spire.identity: "spiffe://cluster.local/ns/default/sa/spark-sa"
spec:
  serviceAccountName: spark-sa
  containers:
  - name: spark
    image: myrepo/spark:latest
```

```yaml
# Noncompliant Pod (no SPIRE identity)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: noncompliant-spark
spec:
  containers:
  - name: spark
    image: myrepo/spark:latest
```

## Validation Plan
- Deploy constraint template and constraint; attempt compliant pod deployment; verify admission allows and audit sidecar is injected. 
- Deploy noncompliant pod; confirm admission denies with clear event reason. 
- Run a Spark job and inspect API calls logged by the auditing sidecar for traceability.
